sam: Quick flag - onboarding run for ranky-7b-lite shows NDCG@10 down ~1.9% vs baseline on the curated holdout, but MRR@10 up ~1.2%. Looks like a quality shift, not just variance. Any ideas?
lina: Do we have cohort breakdown? Head vs tail? My money is on document trimming or candidate-snippet changes during preprocessing.
omar: I pulled per-cohort metrics. Short-query head cohort: ndcg +0.3% mrr +1.4%. Long-doc tail cohort: ndcg -3.8% mrr -0.2%.
beth: Command I used to reproduce: `./tools/eval_rerank --model ranky-7b-lite --set holdout_curated --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10,p@1 --seed 123`
sam: Thanks. We switched default snippet length from 256->192 in that bring-up PR to reduce compute. Could be losing context for long-doc items.
lina: Also note we applied a new doc-casing normalizer which collapses URLs and removes duplicate punctuation. That could change tokenization boundaries.
eval-bot: scheduled-scan: running ablation matrix (snippet_len=256/192, normalizer=old/new, quant=fp16/int8). run id rb-3350. ETA 25m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
omar: While we wait, I ran a small sample diff across 200 queries. Score RMSE of rank positions between baseline and candidate is 0.42 overall, but 1.3 on long-doc tail.
beth: Do we have embed drift? Maybe encoder output changed due to tokenization which affects dot product distribution and thus NDCG more than MRR.
sam: Good point. Also check candidate pruning behavior - we tightened dedupe threshold last week which might remove near-duplicates and reshuffle order. That often hurts NDCG while boosting P@1 for topical queries.
lina: If pruning/dedupe is involved, we'd see more candidate-level churn at positions 3-10. Can someone dump confusions for a handful of regressions?
omar: I'll prepare a CSV with query_id, baseline_ranklist, new_ranklist, delta_ndcg.
eval-bot: ablation results in:
```
snippet=256 normalizer=old quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4271 mrr@10 0.2198
snippet=192 normalizer=old quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4205 mrr@10 0.2222
snippet=256 normalizer=new quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4236 mrr@10 0.2210
snippet=192 normalizer=new quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4183 mrr@10 0.2234
snippet=256 normalizer=old quant=int8  -> ndcg@10 0.4259 mrr@10 0.2201
snippet=192 normalizer=old quant=int8  -> ndcg@10 0.4189 mrr@10 0.2229
snippet=256 normalizer=new quant=int8  -> ndcg@10 0.4218 mrr@10 0.2220
snippet=192 normalizer=new quant=int8  -> ndcg@10 0.4162 mrr@10 0.2241
```
beth: So both shorter snippets and the new normalizer reduce NDCG independently, and quantization (int8) slightly exaggerates the NDCG drop but also nudges MRR up. Pattern consistent with losing context and thresholding noise that affects tail rank order.
sam: Actionable: 1) Re-run with snippet_len=224 as a middle ground and evaluate long-doc tail specifically. 2) Run targeted candidate churn analysis for top 10 positions on affected queries (omar). 3) Try int8 eval with snippet=224 to see combined effect.
lina: I'll add a config toggle so we can A/B snippet length per-customer to see production impact without full rollback.
omar: Uploaded churn CSV to the thread: 14 queries with >3 position shifts concentrated in topic clusters 'api-auth' and 'cli-errors'.
beth: For model onboarding doc, note we should include a checklist: cohort slicing (short/long), snippet-length sensitivity, dedupe threshold, tokenizer/normalizer parity, and quant-scan. This would have caught this earlier.
sam: Agree. I'll open a quick RFC to add that to the onboarding checklist. Also marking this run with a hold: no canary until we stabilize NDCG on long-docs.
eval-bot: note: hold flag set for model ranky-7b-lite (reason: ndcg regression on holdout_longdoc >1%).
lina: Great. Omar, please link the 20 example queries in the RFC. Let's reconvene after the 224 run. :calendar:
omar: Will do, ETA results ~40m.
